questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) If one wishes to comprehend the structural shifts in macroeconomic theory / (2) that occurred following the collapse of the Bretton Woods system, / (3) you must analyze the divergence between fixed exchange rates / (4) and the adoption of fiat currency models by major industrial nations.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) If one wishes to comprehend the structural shifts in macroeconomic theory / (2) that occurred following the collapse of the Bretton Woods system, / (3) you must analyze the divergence between fixed exchange rates / (4) and the adoption of fiat currency models by major industrial nations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. you must analyze .

Key Points

  • The given sentence contains a grammatical inconsistency in pronoun usage. The pronoun "one" is used in part (1), whereas part (3) uses "you", leading to a mismatch in the sentence's point of view.
  • When "one" is used as the pronoun, consistency requires that it be used throughout the sentence.
  • To correct the error, replace "you must analyze" in part (3) with "one must analyze."

Correct sentence: If one wishes to comprehend the structural shifts in macroeconomic theory that occurred following the collapse of the Bretton Woods system, one must analyze the divergence between fixed exchange rates and the adoption of fiat currency models by major industrial nations.

Additional Information

  • Consistency in Pronouns:
    • Pronouns like "one," "you," "he," etc., must remain consistent throughout the sentence to maintain clarity and grammatical accuracy.
    • Mixing pronouns leads to ambiguity and is considered incorrect.
  • Common Errors with Pronoun Usage:
    • Switching between "one" and "you" in formal writing.
    • Using "they" as a singular pronoun without context in formal writing.

questions.question: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect speech. "When are you leaving?" He asked
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect speech.
"When are you leaving?" He asked

options.text: He asked to me when will I be leaving?
options.html: He asked to me when will I be leaving?

options.text: He asked when would I be leaving?
options.html: He asked when would I be leaving?

options.text: He asked when I was leaving.
options.html: He asked when I was leaving.

options.text: He asked when will I have left.
options.html: He asked when will I have left.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'He asked when I was leaving.'

Key Points

  • While changing the narration of an interrogative sentence in the present continuous tense into the affirmative sentence in the reported form we make the following changes
  • The quotation marks get omitted and the question mark gets replaced by a full stop.
  • When the question in the direct speech begins with WH question then conjunction "that" is not used as the "question word" itself acts as a joining clause.
  • The present continuous tense of the question in the direct speech changes to the past continuous tense in the indirect speech.
    • The correct sentence is 'He asked when I was leaving.'

​Additional Information​

  • Let us explore some examples of narrations:
S.No Direct Speech Indirect Speech
1 "I always had bread and butter for breakfast", he said He said that he always had bread and butter for breakfast.
2 "I am washing utensils", she replied. She replied that she was washing utensils.
3 "She resigned on Saturday", the boss informed me. The boss informed me that she had resigned on Saturday.


Hinglish

  • Present continuous tense में एक interrogative वाक्य के narration को रिपोर्ट किए गए रूप में affirmative वाक्य में बदलते समय हम निम्नलिखित परिवर्तन करते हैं।
  • Quotation marks हटा दिए जाते हैं और question mark को full stop से बदल दिया जाता है।
  • जब direct speech में प्रश्न WH प्रश्न से शुरू होता है तो conjunction "that" का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है तथा "प्रश्न शब्द" स्वयं में joining clause के रूप में कार्य करता है।
  • Direct speech में प्रश्न का present continuous tense, indirect speech में past continuous tense में बदल जाता है।
    • सही वाक्य है 'He asked when I was leaving.'

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Pleasure cannot derive from giving pain to innocent people.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Pleasure cannot derive from giving pain to innocent people.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is 'Pleasure cannot derive'.

Key Points

  • The segment that contains the grammatical error is "Pleasure cannot derive."
  • The correct word usage would be: "Pleasure cannot be derived."
  • The corrected sentence would read: "Pleasure cannot be derived from giving pain to innocent people."
  • The error lies in the structure of the verb. In the original sentence, "derive" is intransitive, meaning it doesn't take an object directly following it. Instead, it usually requires a preposition like "from" to connect it to the source of what pleasure is gained from. To rectify this, we use the passive construction "Pleasure cannot be derived," which requires the addition of the auxiliary verb "be" to form the passive voice.
  • Here's a more detailed breakdown:
    • "Derive" is a transitive verb that often requires a preposition like "from" to link it to what something is obtained or gained from. For example: "She derives joy from her hobbies."
    • However, in the passive voice, we need to add the auxiliary verb "be" to form the passive construction: "Pleasure cannot be derived from giving pain to innocent people."
  • In the corrected sentence, the passive voice ("Pleasure cannot be derived") is used to appropriately convey that pleasure cannot be obtained from causing pain to innocent people.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence. After her husband passed away, Jane had to learn to bite the bullet and take care of the household on her own.

The correct answer is: Accept a difficult situation bravely.

Key Points

  • The phrase "bite the bullet" means to face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage and determination. (कठिन परिस्थिति का साहसपूर्वक सामना करना)
    • Example: Despite the pain, he decided to bite the bullet and finish the marathon.
  • "Accept a difficult situation bravely" refers to acknowledging a tough situation and dealing with it courageously. (कठिन परिस्थिति को बहादुरी से स्वीकार करना)
    • Example: After losing his job, he had to accept the difficult situation bravely and start looking for new opportunities.
  • Hence, we can infer that the phrase 'bite the bullet' means to 'accept a difficult situation bravely'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Accept a difficult situation bravely.

questions.question: Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word. If the spelling is already correct, choose "No replacement required." The professor’s exagerated claims about the archaeological site were met with skepticism by the scientific community.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word. If the spelling is already correct, choose "No replacement required."

The professor’s exagerated claims about the archaeological site were met with skepticism by the scientific community.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Exaggerated.

Key Points

  • The word "exagerated" is incorrectly spelled. The correct spelling is "exaggerated".
  • Exaggerated means something that is overstated or described as greater than it actually is. (अतिशयोक्ति पूर्ण)
    • Example: The media often gives exaggerated accounts of celebrity lifestyles.

Correct word explanation: The word "exaggerated" is used to describe something that is made to seem larger, more important, or more extreme than it really is. (अतिशयोक्ति पूर्ण)

  • Example: His claims about his wealth were clearly exaggerated to impress others.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Exaggerated.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Exageratted (गलत वर्तनी): This is an incorrect spelling and does not have any meaning.
  • Exaggeratted (गलत वर्तनी): This is also an incorrect spelling of the word "exaggerated."
  • No replacement required (कोई प्रतिस्थापन आवश्यक नहीं): This option implies that the original word is correct, which is not the case here as the word "exagerated" is misspelled.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) The emergency decree issued by the governor demanded that the municipal authorities / (2) immediately close all low-lying bridges, suspend public transportation, / (3) and should mandate the immediate evacuation of residential zones / (4) vulnerable to catastrophic flash flooding.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) The emergency decree issued by the governor demanded that the municipal authorities / (2) immediately close all low-lying bridges, suspend public transportation, / (3) and should mandate the immediate evacuation of residential zones / (4) vulnerable to catastrophic flash flooding.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. and should mandate the immediate evacuation of residential zones .

Key Points

  • The sentence describes a formal requirement issued by the governor. In such cases, the verbs in the list of demands must maintain parallel structure to ensure grammatical consistency.
  • The verbs in the first two clauses, "demanded that... close" and "suspend", are in the base form, which is appropriate for a subjunctive mood.
  • However, the third part of the sentence uses "should mandate," which introduces unnecessary modal auxiliary ("should") and disrupts the parallel structure.
  • The correct structure would be to use the base form of the verb without "should," making it consistent with the other parts of the sentence.

Correct sentence: The emergency decree issued by the governor demanded that the municipal authorities immediately close all low-lying bridges, suspend public transportation, and mandate the immediate evacuation of residential zones vulnerable to catastrophic flash flooding.

Additional Information

  • Subjunctive Mood:
    • The subjunctive mood is used in formal commands or demands, especially after verbs like demand, suggest, recommend, insist, etc.
    • Structure: The base form of the verb is used after "that."
    • Example: The teacher insisted that the students complete their homework on time.
  • Parallel Structure:
    • When listing items in a series, the grammatical structure of all items must be consistent to ensure clarity and correctness.
    • Example: She likes reading, writing, and painting.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech. "By God!" he cried, "I will not let this injustice stand, let the heavens fall!"
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

"By God!" he cried, "I will not let this injustice stand, let the heavens fall!"

options.text: He swore by God that he would not let that injustice stand, even if the heavens fell.
options.html: He swore by God that he would not let that injustice stand, even if the heavens fell.

options.text: He cried out by God that he will not let this injustice stand, let the heavens fall.
options.html: He cried out by God that he will not let this injustice stand, let the heavens fall.

options.text: He swore solemnly that he would not let that injustice stand, let the heavens fall .
options.html: He swore solemnly that he would not let that injustice stand, let the heavens fall.

options.text: He exclaimed by God that he would not let that injustice stand and let the heavens fall.
options.html: He exclaimed by God that he would not let that injustice stand and let the heavens fall.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. He swore by God that he would not let that injustice stand, even if the heavens fell .

Key Points

  • The given sentence is an example of transforming direct speech into indirect speech.
  • In indirect speech, exclamations and strong emotions are expressed in a more neutral tone.
  • The phrase "By God!" is a strong exclamation, which is transformed to "He swore by God" in indirect speech, retaining the meaning.
  • The use of "would not let" instead of "will not let" is correct in indirect speech because the tense changes to match the reporting verb in the past tense.

Correct sentence: He swore by God that he would not let that injustice stand, even if the heavens fell.

Additional Information

  • Direct Speech vs. Indirect Speech:
    • Direct Speech: Quotes the exact words spoken by a person, e.g., "By God! I will not let this injustice stand."
    • Indirect Speech: Reports the speech in a neutral tone, e.g., He swore by God that he would not let that injustice stand.
    • Usage: Indirect speech is often used for formal or written communication.
  • Tense Change in Indirect Speech:
    • Present tense in direct speech changes to past tense in indirect speech.
    • Example: "He will not let" becomes "He would not let".

questions.question: In the following questions, four alternatives are given for the idioms / phrase underlined in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idioms/phrase. As a leading political figure, he is used to being in the limelight .
questions.questionHtml:
In the following questions, four alternatives are given for the idioms / phrase underlined in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idioms/phrase.

As a leading political figure, he is used to being in the limelight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. "the centre of attraction".

Key Points

  • The phrase "in the limelight" means being at the center of public attention or interest, especially in a positive sense. (सार्वजनिक ध्यान के केंद्र में होना)
    • Example: The actor has been in the limelight ever since his award-winning performance.
  • "The centre of attraction" is the correct interpretation of the phrase "in the limelight," as it denotes being the focus of everyone's attention. (ध्यान का केंद्र)
    • Example: At the party, the birthday girl was the centre of attraction, with everyone gathered around her.
  • Hence, the correct answer is "the centre of attraction."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Giving speeches (भाषण देना): Refers to the act of delivering an address or talk in front of an audience.
    • Example: The professor is known for giving inspiring speeches at conferences.
  • Being criticised (आलोचना झेलना): Refers to receiving negative feedback or judgment for one's actions or decisions.
    • Example: The politician was being criticised for his controversial remarks.
  • Wielding power (शक्ति का प्रयोग करना): Refers to exercising authority or influence over others.
    • Example: The CEO was adept at wielding power to achieve corporate goals.
  • Limelight (चर्चा का केंद्र): Often used to describe someone or something that attracts a lot of attention or focus.
    • Example: The charity event put the organization in the limelight for its good deeds.

questions.question: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Choose the correct option which best expresses the sentence in Passive/Active voice. Where was the match held?
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Choose the correct option which best expresses the sentence in Passive/Active voice.

Where was the match held?

options.text: Where do they hold the match?
options.html: Where do they hold the match?

options.text: Where did they hold the match?
options.html: Where did they hold the match?

options.text: Where were they holding the match?
options.html: Where were they holding the match?

options.text: Where have they hold the match?
options.html: Where have they hold the match?

questions.solution:
Option 2 is the correct answer. 

The sentence is in Passive Voice and in the simple past tense.

It needs to be changed into Active Voice.

On conversion into Active Voice, the given sentence will become: Where did they hold the match?

 

When converting the statement into Active Speech:

1) the object must be written after the subject.

2) the original sentence structure, Object+verb+subject, changes to Subject+verb+object.

3) the tense of the statement is changed accordingly. 

 

Given below are the rules of tense conversion from Active to Passive Voice and vice verse:

TENSE

SENTENCE IN ACTIVE VOICE

SENTENCE IN PASSIVE VOICE

SIMPLE PRESENT

He sells flowers.

He does not sell books.

Does he sell flowers?

Flowers are sold by him.

Books are not sold by him.

Are flowers sold by him?

PRESENT PROGRESSIVE

He is selling flowers.

He is not selling books.

Does he not sell books?

Flowers are being sold by him.

Books are not being sold by him.

Are books not sold by him?

PRESENT PERFECT

He has completed the work.

He has not completed the work.

Has he completed the work?

The work has been completed by him.

The work has not been completed by him.

Has the work been completed by him?

SIMPLE PAST

He completed the work.

He did not complete the work.

 

Did he complete the work?

The work was completed by him.

The work was not completed by him.

Was the work completed by him?

PAST PROGRESSIVE

He was reading a book.

He was not reading a book.

Was he reading a book?

A book was being read by him.

A book was being read by him.

 

Was a book being read by him?

PAST PERFECT

He had read the book

He had not read the book.

Had he read the book?

The book had been read by him.

The book had not been read by him.

Had the book been read by him?

SIMPLE FUTURE

She will write a letter.

She will not write a letter.

 

Will she write the letter?

A letter will be written by her.

A letter will not be written by her.

Will the letter be written by her?

FUTURE PERFECT

He will have written a letter.

He will not have written a letter.

Will he have written a letter?

A letter will have been written by him.

A letter will not have been written by him.

Will a letter have been written by him?

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Somebody stole my favourite shoes.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Somebody stole my favourite shoes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'My favorite shoes were stolen.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the Active Voice.
  • As per the question we have to change it into Passive Voice.
  • The process of transformation as follows:
    • We know that the object "my favourite shoes" will become the subject in the passive voice sentence.
    • The structure of passive voice is:
      • Object of the Active Voice sentence + appropriate form of the verb 'to be' + past participle of the verb + by + subject of the Active Voice sentence (optional)
  • Therefore, the correct passive voice sentence is:
    • "My favourite shoes were stolen."

Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The government is to build a new bridge across the Ganges.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The government is to build a new bridge across the Ganges.

options.text: A new bridge across the Ganges is being built by the government.
options.html: A new bridge across the Ganges is being built by the government.

options.text: A new bridge across the Ganges is built by the government.
options.html: A new bridge across the Ganges is built by the government.

options.text: A new bridge across the Ganges was to be built by the government.
options.html: A new bridge across the Ganges was to be built by the government.

options.text: A new bridge across the Ganges is to be built by the government.
options.html: A new bridge across the Ganges is to be built by the government.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. A new bridge across the Ganges is to be built by the government .

Key Points

  • To convert a sentence from active voice to passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the active voice: "The government is to build a new bridge across the Ganges."
  • In passive voice, the phrase "is to build" becomes "is to be built."
  • The subject "the government" is placed at the end of the sentence, preceded by "by."

Correct sentence: A new bridge across the Ganges is to be built by the government.

Additional Information

  • Common Structure of Passive Voice:
    • Active Voice: Subject + verb + object.
    • Passive Voice: Object + form of "to be" + past participle + (by + subject).
  • Examples:
    • Active: She is writing a book.
    • Passive: A book is being written by her.

questions.question: Consider the following statements: Statement I: Quantum computers can solve certain computational problems exponentially faster than classical computers. Statement II: Quantum computers process information using qubits that can exist in superposition. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements:

Statement I: Quantum computers can solve certain computational problems exponentially faster than classical computers.

Statement II: Quantum computers process information using qubits that can exist in superposition.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I.
options.html: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I.
options.html: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct.
options.html: Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct.

options.text: Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct.
options.html: Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option A.

 

Key Points

  • Quantum computers can solve certain classes of problems such as integer factorisation and specific search problems exponentially or significantly faster than classical computers under appropriate algorithms (e.g., Shor’s algorithm). Hence, Statement I is correct.
  • Quantum computers process information using qubits, which can exist in superposition of states (0 and 1 simultaneously), unlike classical bits that are restricted to either 0 or 1. Hence, Statement II is correct.
  • The principle of superposition, along with entanglement and quantum interference, underpins the computational advantage of quantum systems. Therefore, Statement II explains Statement I.

Thus, both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I → Option A.

Additional Information

  • Quantum advantage depends on algorithmic suitability and error correction.
  • Quantum computing has potential applications in cryptography, material science, and optimization problems.
  • Current quantum systems are in the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) stage.
  • Classical computers remain more practical for most routine computational tasks at present.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution contains provisions related to 'Right against Exploitation'?
questions.questionHtml: <font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;">Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution contains provisions related to 'Right against Exploitation'?</font></font>

options.html: <font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;">Articles 199 and 200</font></font>
<font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;">Articles 45 and 46</font></font>
<font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;">Articles 23 and 24</font></font>
<font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font dir="auto" style="vertical-align: inherit;">Articles 239 and 240</font></font>

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Articles 23 and 24.

Key Points

  • Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution are part of the Fundamental Rights enshrined under Part III of the Constitution.
  • Article 23 prohibits human trafficking, forced labor (begar), and other forms of exploitation, ensuring protection against such practices for every individual in the country.
  • Article 24 specifically prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any other hazardous employment.
  • These articles aim to uphold human dignity and ensure that citizens are not subjected to inhumane treatment or exploitation.
  • These provisions are fundamental to achieving social justice and protecting vulnerable groups in India.

Additional Information

  • Articles 199 and 200
    • These articles are part of the legislative procedures in the Constitution of India.
    • Article 199 pertains to the definition of "money bills" and outlines their scope and content in the legislative process.
    • Article 200 deals with the governor's assent to bills, including the power to withhold assent, reserve the bill for the President's consideration, or return the bill (other than money bills) for reconsideration by the legislature.
  • Articles 45 and 46
    • These articles fall under the Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.
    • Article 45 originally mandated the state to provide free and compulsory education to children below the age of 14 years. After the 86th Amendment (2002), this is now addressed under Article 21A, and Article 45 focuses on early childhood care and education for children below six years.
    • Article 46 directs the state to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and other weaker sections.
  • Articles 239 and 240
    • These articles relate to the administration of Union Territories (UTs).
    • Article 239 provides for the administration of UTs by the President of India through an appointed administrator.
    • Article 240 grants the President the power to make regulations for certain Union Territories, including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep, in the absence of a legislature.

questions.question: In the context of recent developments in space biotechnology, the terms Chlorella sorokiniana-I, Parachlorella kessleri-I and Dysmorphococcus globosus-HI refer to:
questions.questionHtml: In the context of recent developments in space biotechnology, the terms Chlorella sorokiniana-I, Parachlorella kessleri-I and Dysmorphococcus globosus-HI refer to:

options.text: Genetically modified cyanobacteria engineered for enhanced nitrogen fixation in agricultural systems.

options.html: Species of microalgae investigated in space-based experiments, including studies conducted aboard the International Space Station.

options.html: Thermophilic bacteria isolated from hydrothermal vent ecosystems in deep oceans.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option B.

 

Key Points

  • Space biotechnology involves studying biological organisms in microgravity environments to understand how life processes behave in space.
  • Microorganisms such as microalgae are of particular interest because they can contribute to life-support systems, oxygen generation, carbon dioxide recycling, and food production during long-duration space missions.
  • Chlorella sorokiniana-I is a species of green microalgae studied for its high photosynthetic efficiency and ability to produce oxygen and biomass in controlled environments. It has been investigated in space-based biological experiments. Hence, this supports Option B.
  • Parachlorella kessleri-I is another microalgal species belonging to the Chlorella group, known for rapid growth and high carbon fixation capacity. Such species are studied in microgravity conditions to assess their role in closed-loop life-support systems for astronauts. Hence, this also supports Option B.
  • Dysmorphococcus globosus-HI is a microalga species investigated in space biology research, including experiments related to photosynthesis, carbon recycling, and oxygen production in space habitats.

These organisms are therefore microalgae studied in space-based biotechnology experiments, including research carried out on the International Space Station (ISS).

Thus, these terms refer to microalgae species investigated in space experiments → Option B.

Additional Information

  • Microalgae are considered promising for Bioregenerative Life Support Systems (BLSS) in space missions.
  • Potential roles of microalgae in space missions:
    • Oxygen production through photosynthesis
    • Carbon dioxide removal
    • Food and nutrient production
    • Waste recycling

Microalgae species such as Chlorella and Spirulina are often studied due to:

  • High photosynthetic efficiency
  • Rapid biomass production
  • Ability to grow in closed ecological systems

The International Space Station (ISS) serves as a platform for experiments studying how microgravity affects biological growth, metabolism, and genetic regulation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements, in the context of Indian citizenship provisions, is correct? I) Citizenship is listed in the State list. I I) Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution of India deal with various categories of persons who are entitled to citizenship. III) There are only three ways to get Indian citizenship.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements, in the context of Indian citizenship provisions, is correct?

I) Citizenship is listed in the State list. I

I) Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution of India deal with various categories of persons who are entitled to citizenship.

III) There are only three ways to get Indian citizenship.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2: Only II.

Key Points

  • Citizenship in India is covered under Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution of India and deals with the different categories of persons who are entitled to citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
  • Citizenship is not listed in the State List; it is in the Union List under the Seventh Schedule, making it a subject under the exclusive jurisdiction of the central government.
  • Indian citizenship can be acquired through five ways: birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory, as per the Citizenship Act, 1955.
  • The Constitution provided initial provisions for citizenship, and subsequent changes have been made through amendments to the Citizenship Act.
  • Correct statement here is "Articles 5 to 11 deal with various categories of persons entitled to citizenship," which aligns with the provisions in the Constitution.

Additional Information

  • Indian Citizenship Act, 1955
    • This Act governs the acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship.
    • It lays down five modes of acquiring citizenship: birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
    • It also provides provisions for the termination and renunciation of citizenship.
  • Union List vs State List
    • The Union List contains subjects of national importance on which only the central government can make laws, including citizenship, defense, foreign affairs, and atomic energy.
    • State List contains matters on which state governments can legislate, such as police, public health, and agriculture.
  • Dual Citizenship
    • India does not allow dual citizenship. Indian citizens cannot hold citizenship of another country simultaneously.
    • However, the Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) status provides certain rights to foreign nationals of Indian origin.
  • Amendments to Citizenship Act
    • The Citizenship Act has been amended several times, including the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, which provides citizenship to persecuted minorities from Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.
    • This amendment has sparked debates around secularism and equality in India.

questions.question: Match the following bodies with their constitutional status in Uttar Pradesh: List-I (Body) List-II (Status) A. State Finance Commission 1. Non-Constitutional body B. Lokayukta 2. Constitutional (State) C. UP Public Service Commission 3. Constitutional (Central provision) D. State Information Commission 4. Statutory body
questions.questionHtml:
Match the following bodies with their constitutional status in Uttar Pradesh:

List-I (Body)                                   List-II (Status)
A. State Finance Commission 1. Non-Constitutional body
B. Lokayukta 2. Constitutional (State)
C. UP Public Service Commission 3. Constitutional (Central provision)
D. State Information Commission 4. Statutory body
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.

Key Points

  • State Finance Commission:
    • The State Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under Article 243-I of the Indian Constitution.
    • It is responsible for recommending the distribution of financial resources between the state and local bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities).
    • Hence, its status is constitutional (State).
  • Lokayukta:
    • The Lokayukta is a non-constitutional body established by a state law, and its functioning is governed by the Lokayukta Act passed by the respective state legislature.
    • It is primarily an ombudsman authority to investigate corruption and maladministration complaints against public officials.
    • Hence, its status is non-constitutional body.
  • UP Public Service Commission:
    • The UP Public Service Commission (UPPSC) is a constitutional body formed under Article 315 and subsequent provisions of the Indian Constitution.
    • It is responsible for recruiting candidates for various state-level civil services.
    • Its status is constitutional (Central provision).
  • State Information Commission:
    • The State Information Commission is a statutory body established under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
    • Its primary role is to ensure transparency and accountability in public administration.
    • Hence, its status is statutory body.

Additional Information

  • State Finance Commission:
    • Each state is mandated to constitute the State Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats and Municipalities.
    • The recommendations of the commission are advisory in nature and assist the state government in allocating resources effectively.
  • Lokayukta:
    • The Lokayukta is modeled after the Ombudsman system in Scandinavian countries.
    • Its scope and powers vary from state to state as it is governed by state-specific legislation.
    • It helps in investigating corruption cases involving ministers, legislators, and bureaucrats.
  • UP Public Service Commission:
    • Established under the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935, the commission continues to function under the Indian Constitution.
    • It conducts various state-level examinations such as PCS (Provincial Civil Services) and ACF/RFO (Assistant Conservator of Forest/Range Forest Officer).
  • State Information Commission:
    • The Right to Information Act, 2005 enables citizens to seek information from public authorities, ensuring transparency.
    • The State Information Commission is responsible for hearing appeals and complaints regarding the RTI Act's implementation.
    • It aims to promote accountability in public offices through the dissemination of information.

Important Points

  • Key Articles of the Constitution:
    • Article 243-I: Deals with the formation of State Finance Commissions for Panchayats and Municipalities.
    • Article 315: Provides for the establishment of Public Service Commissions for the Union and the States.
  • Statutory vs Constitutional Bodies:
    • Constitutional bodies are established by provisions of the Constitution (e.g., State Finance Commission, UPPSC).
    • Statutory bodies are established by an act of Parliament or State Legislature (e.g., State Information Commission).
    • Non-constitutional bodies are created by executive orders or specific laws (e.g., Lokayukta).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

Key Points

  • Chandragupta II was one of the most powerful emperors of the Gupta Empire in India.
  • He adopted the title 'Vikramaditya', which signifies valor and is associated with a legendary king of ancient India.
  • His reign is often considered a golden age of cultural and scholarly achievements in ancient India.
  • Renowned scholars and poets such as Kalidasa and Amarasimha were part of his court.
  • Chandragupta II's rule was marked by significant advancements in science, art, and literature.

Additional Information

  • Gupta Empire:
    • The Gupta Empire existed from approximately 320 to 550 CE and is known for its significant contributions to arts, science, and political organization.
    • This period is often referred to as the Golden Age of India due to its advancements and prosperity.
  • Kalidasa:
    • He was a classical Sanskrit writer, widely regarded as the greatest poet and dramatist in the Sanskrit language.
    • Notable works include 'Shakuntala,' 'Meghaduta,' and 'Raghuvamsha.'
  • Amarasimha:
    • He was an ancient Indian scholar and author of the 'Amarakosha,' a lexicon in Sanskrit.
    • The 'Amarakosha' is an important source for understanding classical Sanskrit and Indian culture.
  • Vikramaditya:
    • The title 'Vikramaditya' is often used by Indian kings to signify their valor and heroism.
    • Chandragupta II's adoption of this title reflected his status and achievements.
  • Golden Age of India:
    • This term refers to a period of great cultural, scientific, and economic prosperity in Indian history.
    • The Gupta period is considered the epitome of this era.

  • Their capital was Uraiyur (near Tiruchirapalli town) and Puhar or Kaviripattinam was an alternative royal residence and chief port town. Hence, Pair 2 is correctly matched.
  • Tiger was their emblem.

Pandyas:

  • Korkai was their main port, located near the confluence of Thampraparani with the Bay of Bengal. It was famous for pearl fishery and chank diving.

  • They adopted the Vedic religion of sacrifice and patronized Brahmin priests.

    • Sadra was not called "Diwan-a-Sadat" while conducting judicial work. In fact, Sadra was responsible for religious and charitable endowments, education, and overseeing religious scholars. The term "Diwan" generally referred to a financial officer or minister, not a judicial one.

Additional Information

  • Vizarat
    • The Vizarat was an important institution in the Mughal administrative system. The Vizier (Wazir) held significant power and was responsible for the administration of the empire.
    • The Vizier's role included managing the state finances, overseeing provincial administration, and advising the emperor on policy matters.
  • Sadra
    • Sadra was a high-ranking official responsible for religious and educational institutions. They managed waqfs (charitable endowments), madrasas (educational institutions), and religious scholars.
    • Sadra played a key role in promoting Islamic education and welfare activities within the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about the Buddhist architecture in the Gandhara region?
questions.questionHtml: Which statement is correct about the Buddhist architecture in the Gandhara region?

options.text: Some stupas had swastika carved on their base
options.html: Some stupas had swastika carved on their base

options.text: Ayaaka platforms and pillars are found.
options.html: Ayaaka platforms and pillars are found.

options.text: Indian and Greek features and styles are intertwined.
options.html: Indian and Greek features and styles are intertwined.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indian and Greek features and styles are intertwined.

Key Points

  •  The Buddhist architecture of the Gandhara region, which flourished from the 1st century BCE to the 5th century CE in present-day northwest Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan, is renowned for its unique synthesis of Indian and Hellenistic (Greek) artistic and architectural styles.
  • This fusion arose from the historical interactions between the Indian subcontinent and the Greek successor states following Alexander the Great's conquests.
  • The Gandhara school of art and architecture developed under the patronage of various rulers, including the Indo-Greeks, Scythians, Parthians, and Kushans, who facilitated cultural exchange between the regions.
  • One of the most distinctive characteristics of Gandhara Buddhist architecture is the prominent influence of Greek artistic elements in the depiction of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas.
  • Sculptures often feature realistic human forms with Greco-Roman features such as wavy hair, draped robes reminiscent of togas, and serene facial expressions influenced by Hellenistic sculpture.
  • Architectural elements also reflect Greek influence, with the use of Corinthian columns, acanthus leaf decorations, and classical architectural orders in the construction of monasteries and stupas.
  • However, these Greek elements were seamlessly integrated with traditional Indian Buddhist architectural principles and decorative motifs.
  • Stupas in the Gandhara region typically featured a stepped pyramidal structure for the dome (anda), a departure from the more hemispherical shape found in other parts of India.

questions.question: Which of the following styles of paintings are also known for Panchatantra Paintings?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following styles of paintings are also known for Panchatantra Paintings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Marwar.

Key Points

  • Panchatantra style is also known as the Marwari style of paintings.
  • Panchatantra literally means five treaties.
  • It is an ancient collection of animal fables, the animals have human virtues and vices.

Additional Information

  • Bundi Style:
    • Bundi style developed during the times of Rao Surjan Singh.
    • The location of Bundi was such that it favoured the immigration of the artists from all sides.
    • Bundi painting is an important school of the Rajasthani style of Indian miniature painting that originated in the princely state of Bundi, located between Jaipur and Udaipur.
    • The blend of Mughal and Deccani art elements in Bundi style is unique.
    • The main subjects of these paintings are Krishna Leela, Rama Leela, Baramasa, hunting scenes, scenes of court, festivals, elephants, horses, battle scenes, horse races, flowers, trees, etc.
  • Kota style:
    • It refers to painting from the small court of Kota from the seventeenth century to the nineteenth century.
    • The Mughals established Kota as an independent state from Bundi to be ruled by a branch of the family in 1631 and stylistically, the early art of Kota followed the Bundi model and concentrated on Ragamala and Baramasa painting.
  • Dhundhar style:
    • Dhundhar is a historical region of Rajasthan.
    • It includes the districts of Jaipur, Sawai Madhopur, and Tonk.
    • Dhundar style of paintings had continued its pace of development through various new forms from time to time.
    • This painting style was developed by the Hada Rajput rulers in the Bundi and Kota regions.
    • The miniature paintings of these two centers are superb creations and typically portray beautiful women with round faces, large eyes, long necks, and pointed noses.
    • The haunting activities of the erstwhile ruler and emperors are depicted in these paintings.

  • It has two prominent gateways known as Kolepalli Darwaza and Nadella Darwaza.
  • Kondaveedu Fort is also known for its sophisticated water conservation system consisting of ponds and reservoirs.
  • Archaeological findings in the region include Buddhist stupa remains dating to the 1st–2nd century CE, indicating earlier Buddhist presence in the area.

Consider the following statements regarding the “Moonshot” Project:

Statement I: The “Moonshot” Project is a national programme launched by the Government of India to develop reusable launch vehicles and next-generation lunar exploration technologies.

Statement II: The project launched by the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) aims to develop brain co-processors that decode neural signals using artificial intelligence to help restore lost brain functions.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4

In News

  • The Indian Institute of Science (IISc) recently launched the Moonshot Project, an advanced research initiative aimed at developing brain co-processors using neuromorphic hardware and artificial intelligence to restore lost neurological functions.

Key Points

    • The “Moonshot Project” recently in news refers to an IISc-led brain co-processor project, not a Government of India space programme. IISc describes it as a project to develop implantable and non-invasive brain co-processors that can decode brain activity, process it through AI algorithms, and help restore or enhance brain functions.
    • Statement I: The Government of India has approved work on reusable or partially reusable space launch technologies such as the Next Generation Launch Vehicle, but this is not the “Moonshot Project” referred to here. Hence, Statement I is incorrect.

    • Therefore, the highlighted answer Option 2 is incorrect. The correct answer is Option 4.

  • It plans to develop implantable and non-invasive neural co-processors for neurological rehabilitation.
  • The project will also create India-specific stereo EEG and ECoG datasets as digital public goods.
  • Development is planned in two phases: a non-invasive neural co-processor followed by a minimally invasive embedded implant.

questions.question: Which of the following substances are NOT in the list of ODSs (Ozone Depleting Substances)?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following substances are NOT in the list of ODSs (Ozone Depleting Substances)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is SO3.

Key Points

  • SO3 (Sulfur Trioxide) is not classified as an Ozone Depleting Substance (ODS).
  • ODSs are primarily substances that contain chlorine, bromine, or fluorine, which react with ozone in the stratosphere, leading to ozone depletion.
  • SO3 is a precursor to sulfuric acid and does not contain any ozone-depleting elements like chlorine or bromine.
  • SO3 is associated with the formation of acid rain when combined with water vapor, but it does not impact the ozone layer directly.
  • Its environmental impact is primarily related to air pollution and acidification of ecosystems, rather than ozone depletion.

Additional Information

  • CFCs (Chlorofluorocarbons)
    • CFCs are one of the most well-known Ozone Depleting Substances (ODSs) due to their high ozone depletion potential (ODP).
    • They are synthetic compounds made of chlorine, fluorine, and carbon and were widely used as refrigerants, propellants, and solvents.
    • When released into the atmosphere, CFCs rise to the stratosphere where UV radiation causes them to release chlorine atoms, which then destroy ozone molecules.
    • The Montreal Protocol (1987) was established to phase out the production and use of CFCs globally.
  • CH3Br (Methyl Bromide)
    • CH3Br is a brominated compound that is classified as an ODS with significant ozone depletion potential.
    • It was mainly used as a fumigant in agriculture to control pests and as a soil sterilant.
    • Bromine released from CH3Br is far more effective at destroying ozone than chlorine.
    • Efforts under the Montreal Protocol have reduced its use significantly, although some exemptions exist for critical agricultural uses.
  • Halons
    • Halons are compounds that contain bromine, fluorine, and carbon, and are used primarily in fire suppression systems.
    • They are highly effective at extinguishing fires but are also extremely potent ODSs due to the bromine content.
    • Halons have been phased out under the Montreal Protocol, although certain critical uses (e.g., in aircraft fire suppression) still persist.
    • Replacements for halons, such as hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), are being developed to reduce environmental impact.
